title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## Perceptive Multi‑Skill Humanoid Locomotion

### The Breakthrough
The authors present a two‑layer architecture that plans whole‑body motions directly from raw depth images and tracks them with a reinforcement‑learning‑trained policy. A perceptive flow‑matching motion generator creates trajectories, while an off‑policy fine‑tuning loop improves it, boosting terrain‑traversal success by up to 25 pp and skill selection by up to 80 pp. The system runs on a real Unitree G1 humanoid using only two depth cameras and succeeds on outdoor obstacles such as boxes and stairs.

### The Caveats
The paper names no baseline methods or standard benchmarks, so the significance of the reported gains cannot be assessed.

## LeCo Compliance Insertion

### The Breakthrough
LeCo couples visual policy learning with a fixed admittance controller, converting high‑frequency contact data into multirate reward signals that penalize pushing against compliance. Experiments on four real connector‑assembly tasks achieve a 94 % success rate and noticeably lower peak force/torque values.

### The Caveats
The reported performance lacks comparison to existing adaptive‑compliance or baseline insertion approaches.

## CeDiRNet‑6DoF Cloth Unfolding

### The Breakthrough
CeDiRNet‑6DoF jointly learns dense 3D grasp regression, segmentation, and sine‑cosine encoded Euler angles to output full 6‑DoF grasp poses that maximize unfolded cloth area. Evaluated on a bimanual robot in the ICRA 2024 Cloth Competition, it attains state‑of‑the‑art results.

### The Caveats
The claimed superiority is unsupported because the paper provides no baseline comparisons.

## STL‑SVPG Sparse‑Reward RL

### The Breakthrough
STL‑SVPG embeds Signal Temporal Logic robustness into Stein Variational Policy Gradient, enabling trajectory‑level credit assignment for sparse‑success tasks. It achieves the highest mean success on five of six quadcopter and manipulator benchmarks and demonstrates sim‑to‑real transfer.

### The Caveats
No prior baselines are named or compared against, leaving the claimed state‑of‑the‑art status unverified.

## Canadarm2 ISS Issue

### The Breakthrough
Canadarm2’s modular inchworm architecture with identical ends has operated for over 20 years; after a routine walk‑off maneuver, the arm remains functional and is used to inspect the Crew‑12 Dragon despite communication errors in its mobile transporter.

### The Caveats
The robustness claim is unsubstantiated, as no root‑cause analysis of the communication errors has been presented.

## Tesla Optimus V3 Production

### The Breakthrough
Optimus V3 features highly dexterous hands assembled from more than 100 components and integrates AI‑driven control, with Tesla targeting a weekly output of over 1,000 units by the end of 2026.

### The Caveats
The story provides only production‑throughput targets and no independent evidence of the robots’ real‑world manipulation ability, safety, or performance.

## Roborock Offline Cloud Hack

### The Breakthrough
The hack rewrites the firmware‑hardcoded hostname to redirect traffic to a user‑controlled server, then recovers the vacuum’s public key via an RSA‑signature GCD attack, enabling full offline control through Home Assistant without rooting.

### The Caveats
The solution is demonstrated on only a few Roborock units, so its generality across the product line is unclear.

## Spirula Studio 3D Gaussian Splatting

### The Breakthrough
Spirula Studio is a single‑binary C++ tool that trains 3D Gaussian splatting models up to 10 M SH‑3 Gaussians in 8 GB VRAM using a cross‑vendor Vulkan (or CUDA) backend, with built‑in SfM, 360° camera support, and a GUI viewer.

### The Caveats
Performance claims are unverified; the repository offers no benchmark results or comparisons to existing splatting pipelines.

### What to watch
Three papers tackle manipulation from different angles: LeCo focuses on compliant insertion via reward‑shaped visual policies, CeDiRNet‑6DoF advances vision‑based 6‑DoF grasp estimation for deformable cloth, and STL‑SVPG introduces temporal‑logic‑guided RL for sparse‑reward tasks. Together they illustrate a trend toward tighter integration of perception, compliance, and high‑level task specifications.

### Priority
The perceptive humanoid locomotion system is the most compelling start today because it demonstrates a complete perception‑to‑control pipeline on a real robot, delivering measurable outdoor navigation gains with minimal sensor hardware.

### One action
If you have a depth‑camera equipped robot, replicate the two‑camera setup and test the flow‑matching motion generator using the authors’ released code.
